D17E_T_WHAT_KEBAB: [proudly] [excited] I taught him kebab. Skewers instead of stakes. [beaming] I did a good deed!
D17E_T_WHAT_LEGEND: [sheepish] I told a story. With a vampire. [nervous] He took notes.
D17E_T_WHAT_NONE: [defensive] [shouting] Nothing! I didn't interfere! [sheepish] I just got a bit wet.
D17E_T_WHAT_POLICY: [proudly] I sold a policy. To Vlad. [nervous] He… [wincing] liked the stake.
D17E_V_01: [cold] [proud] My father is the dragon. I am the dragon's son: Drăculea. [contemptuous] And who are you, wet one?
D17E_V_02: [bitter] [flat] Father left us here. Now we hear he's joining the crusaders. [darkly] I wonder whether the sultan will kill us.
D17E_V_04: [sullen] You like everywhere, Radu. [quietly] [homesick] I only like home.
D17E_V_BURN: [flat] [annoyed] Turn them. Or we eat charcoal.
D17E_V_KEB_0: [flat] Here. Sharp. [suspicious] If that's what you want.
D17E_V_KEB_2: [dreamy] [darkly] One day I'll make a whole forest of skewers.
D17E_V_LEG: [disgusted] Blood? Disgusting. [pause] [intrigued] But… are people afraid of him?
D17E_V_NONE: [cold] [staring] Were you going to say something, wet one?
D17E_V_POL: [skeptical] [slowly] So I give you gold, you give me a paper. [suspicious] And if something happens… clause 9?
D17E_V_POL_3: [deadpan] A stake. Through the purse. [slow smile] I like it. [darkly amused] I'll stake everyone.
D20O_U_EDIRNE_OK: [gruff] [proud] The ball that landed at the foot of the post in Edirne came out of this barrel. [fatherly] The bronze is sound, lad; keep your hands sound too.
D20O_U_EDIRNE_SHORT: [gruff] [worried] Remember the short shot in Edirne, lad? The bronze tired there. [grave] Look, a thin line on the barrel's belly: this gun starts the day with a crack.
D26_F_EDIRNE_GREEK: [warm recognition] [slight smile] Sirtaki. [triumphant] As I said: in Constantinople.
D26_F_EDIRNE_HIZIR: [warm recognition] [slight smile] Hızır. [triumphant] As I said: in Constantinople.
D26_F_EDIRNE_TIME: [warm recognition] [slight smile] Lift man. [triumphant] As I said: in Constantinople.
D28O_U_EDIRNE_OK: [gruff] [approving] In Edirne you put the ball at the foot of the post. [warmly] The aim is yours again; you can hold it a little looser this time.
D28O_U_EDIRNE_SHORT: [gruff] [firm] In Edirne the aim was yours, and the ball never reached the post. [commanding] Today I aim. You load, ram and stand back.
D33O_F_EDIRNE_GREEK: [delighted] [laughs] Sirtaki! [teasing] Has your Greek improved? [proudly] Mine has.
D33O_F_EDIRNE_HIZIR: [stunned] You… the pool at Edirne! [delighted] Hızır! [amazed] Eight years, and you haven't aged a day. [awed] So you did find the water of life.
D33O_F_EDIRNE_TIME: [delighted] [laughs] The lift man! Eight years. [amused] I still haven't found the Arabic for it; there's no Persian either.
D30O_Z_01: [commanding] Clerk! You'll carry my ladder. [proud] The palace is there, its lights are on. [determined] By morning we'll be the ones lighting them.
D30O_Z_END: [exhausted] [bitter] Not tonight. This wall didn't fall tonight. [grim] I'll tell the Sultan: the palace side is too high.
D30O_Z_PLANT: [shouting] [commanding] Ladder to the wall! [urgent] Climb! [battle cry] Up!
D30O_Z_RETREAT: [shouting] [urgent] The horn! Back! [desperate] Leave the ladders, don't leave the men!
D21O_Z_01: [confident] If the Sultan can't go over the walls, [smirks] he goes under them. [commanding] Dragan, this man is yours. [dismissive] He's the Bureau's clerk, they say; clerks dig too.
D25_Z_1: [scornful] What fleet? The lookouts have not seen a single sail. [dismissive] The Franks are divided among themselves. [fierce] The walls are crumbling, the army's heart is strong.
D25_Z_2: [firm] So am I. [intense] If we turn back today, we never come again. [resolute] The assault, my Sultan.
D27_Z_01: [loud] [proclaiming] Notables of Galata! Our Sultan has granted his charter to Galata, which opened its gates. [commanding] Listen.
D27_Z_02: [proclaiming] Your houses, shops, vineyards, ships and goods are yours. [firm] No one will touch your wives or your children.
D27_Z_03: [proclaiming] Your churches remain yours; [stern] only no bells will be rung and no new churches built. [measured] You will pay your tax and trade freely by land and sea.
D27_Z_04: [proclaiming] Those who left will have their property returned if they come back. [measured] You will choose an elder from among yourselves to manage your affairs.
D27_Z_05: [stern] Your walls on the landward side will be pulled down and your weapons handed over. [calmer] The sea side may stay; that is the gate of trade.
D33O_Z_01: [impatient] Master! Halil Pasha's tower is two courses ahead of us. [threatening] If this hill falls behind his, you'll hear about it, and so will I.
D25_H_1: [measured] [grave] My Sultan, we have been before these walls for fifty days. [worried] They say a Hungarian army is on the road and a Venetian fleet at sea. [pleading] Let us accept tribute and go home.
D25_H_2: [grave] My Sultan, one defeat can take away the gains of years. [quietly] I am thinking of the state's tomorrow.
CL_BARK_BREAD: [shouting] [cheerful] Bread, warm bread! [proudly] The ovens burn even in a siege!
CL_BARK_CLOTH: [shouting] [salesman voice] Bursa silk, Venetian wool, come and look!
CL_BARK_CURFEW: [stern] No wandering the streets at night. [firm] Go home and bar your door.
CL_BARK_FISH: [shouting] [cheerful] Fresh mackerel! Straight out of the Golden Horn!
CL_BARK_FRUIT: [shouting] [cheerful] Plums, cherries, fresh from the garden!
CL_BARK_HALT: [commanding] [suspicious] Halt! Who are you, where are you going?
CL_BARK_J_MOVE: [shouting] [commanding] Clear the way, patrol coming through!
CL_BARK_J_QUARTER: [firm] This quarter is under the Sultan's protection. [impatient] Move along.
CL_BARK_POTS: [shouting] [salesman voice] Pots and jugs! Nothing better for carrying water!
CL_BARK_WALLS: [impatient] [shouting] The walls need hands to haul stone. Don't stand idle!
D_ARENA_N_B: [over a crackling radio] [formal] "Mr Tolga, this entry is a Bureau drill. It doesn't count towards history. [dry] Hold the breach as long as you can."
D_ARENA_N_O: [over a crackling radio] [formal] "Mr Tolga, this entry is a Bureau drill. It doesn't count towards history. [dry] Hold the slope as long as you can."
D_CLIMB_FALL_1: [pained] Ow! [groaning] I'm up, I'm up. [embarrassed] Nothing broken.
D_CLIMB_FALL_3: [pained] [indignant] That fall was not in the policy.
D_CLIMB_LEAP: [straining] Hup! [out of breath] ...I'm never doing that again. [nervous laugh] I'll probably do it again.
D_CLIMB_TIRED_1: [out of breath] [panting] Breath... my breath... [whining] I was going to sign up for Pilates.
D_CLIMB_TIRED_2: [out of breath] [complaining] This wall wasn't in the policy.
D_CLIMB_TIRED_3: [straining] [whining] My arms were built for holding pens, not walls.
D_FORM_1: [satisfied] [dry] Another form. Even the wind is against bureaucracy.
D_FORM_2: [inspecting] Signature intact. [approving] The seal's damp but valid.
D_FORM_3: [deadpan] A seagull was reading this one. [dry] Looks like it approved.
D_FORM_4: [thoughtful] Forms always flee to high places. [dry] The nature of bureaucracy.
D_FORM_ALL: [satisfied] [proudly] All twelve forms. [dry] I can now write 'no paperwork was lost during flight' in the report.
D_LM_AYASOFYA: [awed] [softly] Hagia Sophia. [dry] A nine-hundred-year-old dome, and it silences you even from above. The Bureau calls it a 'structural risk'. [deadpan] I'd say the Bureau is the structural risk.
D_LM_BLAKHERNA: [thoughtful] Blachernae Palace. The emperor watches the camp from here. [dry] And I'm watching both of them. My jurisdiction just expanded.
D_LM_BOZDOGAN: [impressed] The Aqueduct of Valens. Rome brought water to the city and it's held for a thousand years. [sighs] The tap at our Bureau has been dripping for three weeks.
D_LM_GALATA: [matter-of-fact] Galata Tower. The Genoese built it; here they call it the Tower of Christ. [dry] In six hundred years there'll be a queue for photos. For now, just seagulls.
D_LM_HAVARIYUN: [solemn] The Church of the Holy Apostles. The emperors are buried here. [dry] In a few years another building will rise in its place. [pause] [sighs] No spoilers. Oops.
D_LM_HIPODROM: [thoughtful] The Hippodrome. The obelisk, the Serpent Column... [dry] The chariot races are long gone, but the fans stayed. Blues, Greens. Oddly familiar.
D_LM_KONSTANTIN: [matter-of-fact] The Column of Constantine. There used to be a statue on top; the wind knocked it down in 1106. [deadpan] At the Bureau we call that 'case closed'.
D_LM_SURLAR: [impressed] The Theodosian Walls. [smug] No one has breached them in a thousand years. I just did. [dry] Doesn't count, I'm flying.
D_LM_ZINCIR: [thoughtful] The Golden Horn chain. [grave] Iron links on floating logs. Soon ships will walk overland; the chain isn't ready for that. [quietly] Nobody is.
D_NIHAT_CLOAK_EMPTY: [dry] The veil is recharging. Invisibility is a resource. [formal] It is not to be wasted.
D_NIHAT_CLOAK_OUT: [flat] The veil has run out. I'm visible. [sighs] Regrettably.
D_NIHAT_CLOAK_TALK: [dry] No questioning while invisible. [deadpan] They'd think they were talking to thin air.
D_NIHAT_EDGE: [formal] The field door's range ends here. [dry] Beyond is another file's business.
D_NIHAT_EXPLORE: [reading aloud] A note from Rıza Bey: 'Twelve Z-9 forms went missing on the first flight. Bring them back if you find them.' Those golden lights... [curious] are those the forms?
D_NIHAT_LEGEND: [sighs] [resigned] Five witnesses. That's a legend now. [dry] Legends don't fill in forms, but they do end up in the chronicles.
D_NIHAT_SEEN_1: [alarmed] I've been seen. [reciting] Article 1: an inspector is never seen. I've breached Article 1. [worried] Bureau pressure has gone up.
D_NIHAT_SEYYAH: [satisfied] Nine out of nine. I've finished the travelogue before Evliya Çelebi was even born. [dry] Copyright belongs to the Bureau, naturally.
D_NIHAT_VIEW: [thoughtful] [dry] From up here everything looks like a file: tidy from a distance, a mess up close.
D_NIHAT_VIEW_11: [softly] [thoughtful] The camp at night from above: thousands of fires. All for tomorrow. [concerned] Tolga is sitting by one of them.
D_NIHAT_VIEW_3: [dry] The Bureau's ceiling. Even outside of time there's a ceiling. [deadpan] Regulations.
D_NIHAT_WATER: [annoyed] The forms aren't waterproof. The kit lifted me up on its own. [prim] Regulation: auditors do not get wet.
D_PERCH_AYA: [awed] [softly] I'm on top of the dome. Nine-hundred-year-old lead, warm under my feet. [whispers] One minute... I'm just looking.
D_PERCH_COLUMN: [smug] [dry] Constantine's column. Where the statue stood, now there's an auditor. History corrects itself.
D_PERCH_GALATA: [calm] [content] Galata's gallery. No Genoese sentry, just me. [softly] The Golden Horn laid out like a sheet of paper.
D_WIT_1: [terrified] [shouting] A djinn! A djinn in a fedora!
D_WIT_10: [shocked] [shouting] Good Lord! The tax collector can fly!
D_WIT_2: [awed] [confused] Is that an angel? Why is it wearing a hat?
D_WIT_3: [whispers] [scared] Hasan, did you see that? ...I didn't. [pause] [firmly] And neither did you.
D_WIT_4: [amazed] [shouting] A flying Frank! [laughing nervously] No one's going to believe this!
D_WIT_5: [stunned] If a chronicler wrote this down, nobody would believe it.
D_WIT_8: [nervous] [whispers] Nobody say anything. Just don't look at its face.
D_WIT_9: [stammering] That... that's not a bird. [baffled] Birds don't wear ties.
REACT_CROWD_BYZ_ANY: [amazed] I thought I'd seen everything in Constantinople. [chuckles] I hadn't seen that.
REACT_CROWD_BYZ_CHICKPEAS: [excited] Roasted chickpeas! In a siege they're worth gold. [pleading] Give me a handful and I'll pray for you.
REACT_CROWD_BYZ_COLOGNE: [sniffs] [nostalgic] Lemon! You smell like my late wife. [warmly] That's a good thing, don't worry.
REACT_CROWD_BYZ_CUBE: [curious] A coloured box? [chuckles] My boy would turn this all day; he wouldn't notice if the city fell.
REACT_CROWD_BYZ_LIGHTER: [amazed] Fire in a pocket! A little Greek fire? [eager] Take it to the walls, it'll help.
REACT_CROWD_BYZ_PHONE: [awed] [nervous] This shining stone... is there a saint inside? [whispers] I'd better cross myself.
REACT_CROWD_BYZ_SELFIE: [suspicious] What are you going to do with that stick? [amused] Catch fish, or me?
REACT_CROWD_CAMP_ANY: [shrugging] Frankish stuff. Not my business. [dismissive] Ask the sergeant.
REACT_CROWD_CAMP_CHICKPEAS: [delighted] Chickpeas! [eager] Give me a handful and I'm your man till dawn.
REACT_CROWD_CAMP_COLOGNE: [surprised] Cologne? I haven't washed in three days. [laughs] Go ahead.
REACT_CROWD_CAMP_CUBE: [puzzled] Coloured dice? [skeptical] You can't play backgammon with that.
REACT_CROWD_CAMP_LIGHTER: [amazed] It lights itself! [laughs] If Urban sees it he'll bolt it onto his cannon.
REACT_CROWD_CAMP_PHONE: [suspicious] What's this? There's a voice inside. [nervous] Take it to the imam, let him read over it.
REACT_CROWD_CAMP_SELFIE: [nervous] [lowered voice] A mirror on a stick? Don't let the Agha see, he'll call it sorcery.
REACT_CROWD_GAL_ANY: [shrewd] Everything has a price. [curious] What's this one's?
REACT_CROWD_GAL_CHICKPEAS: [intrigued] Roasted chickpeas? In Genoa this would make a man rich. [eager] Let's be partners.
REACT_CROWD_GAL_COLOGNE: [sniffs] [shrewd] Lemon water or perfume? Whichever it is, double the price.
REACT_CROWD_GAL_CUBE: [delighted] A coloured puzzle! [scheming] I'll sell it to the Venetians and keep them busy for a year.
REACT_CROWD_GAL_LIGHTER: [impressed] A man who carries fire in his pocket! [scheming] We could do the powder trade with this.
REACT_CROWD_GAL_PHONE: [curious] What's this? [haggling] How much? I'll give you a thousand ducats. [quickly] Fine, twelve hundred.
REACT_CROWD_GAL_SELFIE: [amused] Making your own portrait? Florentines hire a painter. [teasing] You hold a stick.
D8_A2_UNKNOWN: [mild] An old man at the hardware store at this hour. Normal. [focused] We're after the garage guy; he never stepped into the light once all night.
D17O_K_COME: [shouting] [excited] Frank! We've emptied the pots and brought the buckets! [commanding] Boys, get in line!
D17O_K_DAWN: [tired] [proud] My pots are empty and my buckets are wet. [chuckles] The Sultan's galley is saved; he owes me a ladle.
D17O_K_DAWN_BURNED: [sighs] The stern burned, but the hull still floats. [wry] Same in the kitchen: the bottom of the pot catches, the meal survives.
D17_G_HELP: [shouting] [urgent] New man! Two of us from Cattaneo's ship. [grateful] On 20 April you cut the ropes at the rail; the captain said "go pay your debt". [determined] We'll hold the rope, you pull!
D17_K_BRIDGE: [gruff] Whatever you are. Mahmud the bridge-builder needs hands; you'll haul barrels and eat his bread. [menacing] Try running and the water's still right there.
D17_K_NET: [surprised] [shouting] Look at the net! Not a fish, a man. [suspicious] Doesn't look Greek, doesn't look Frankish. Who are you, man?
D17_L_CHAIN: [excited] [shouting] Chickpea Frank! Three nights without sleep, and we couldn't if we tried! [urgent] We've got the lantern on them: three heads in the water!
D17_N_CAM_1: [formal] [proudly] The Bureau's recording camera. Model Z-0, instant print. [matter-of-fact] You take the picture, the file prints it.
D17_N_CAM_2: [dry] A phone picture gets deleted, Mr Tolga. [firm] This one drops into your hand, gets signed and goes in the file. Here.
D17_N_CAM_3: [instructive] A test frame. Point it at me; once I'm in the viewfinder, press the shutter.
D17_N_CAM_4: [deadpan] I've closed my eyes. Everyone closes their eyes in a Bureau photograph. [dry] That's how it goes in the file.
D17_N_CAPTIVE: [over a crackling radio] [concerned] Mr Tolga, your signal is coming from the far shore of the Horn. The Bureau can't collect you now: [grave] you'll write one page from the other side. [reassuring] We'll fetch you afterwards.
D17_N_FIRST_36: [formal] One correction, Mr Tolga: the file was opened three weeks earlier. The first entry is 9 April, before dawn. Giustiniani's men are going out beyond the walls, and so are you. [dry] You can run, can't you?
D17_N_LIFT: [calm] Into the lift, Mr Tolga. I'll set the dial; you face the door and breathe.
D17_TR_LOST: [panicked] [shouting] Overboard again! The rope won't reach... [desperate] The guns! Back! Pull back!
D17_TR_SHORT: [urgent] Cattaneo's men have been patching up the carrack since 20 April; they couldn't spare us oarsmen tonight. [tense] We're short-handed, Bureau man. Be quick!
D17_TR_WARN: [angry] [shouting] Fall in again and the rope won't reach you, insurance man! Keep away from the rail!
D17_T_CAM_1: [skeptical] Mr Nihat, this camera is older than my grandfather. [pleading] Can't I just use my phone?
D17_T_CAPTIVE: [nervous laugh] Was there a 'taken prisoner' clause in the policy? There wasn't. [sighs] I know, because I wrote it.
D17_T_CHAIN: [whispers] [disbelief] They ate two. They're still talking.
D17_T_NET: [spluttering] [flustered] I'm in insurance. I mean... a loss assessor. [sheepish] A wet loss assessor.
D18_HA_01: [cheerful] Fez boy! Building a bridge? [friendly] We'll hold the barrels, you tie. Beats guard duty.
D18_HU_01: [confident] I'm Hasan. [confused] ...I'm not. [correcting himself] I'm Hüseyin. And I'm the one holding the barrel.
D18_HU_01_HUFEZ: [proudly] The one in the fez is Hüseyin. That's me. [cheerful] I'll hold the barrel; you tie the rope.
D18_N_01_CAPTIVE: [over a crackling radio] [dry] Mr Tolga, this page is on the Ottoman side, and this time you weren't invited. The boatmen handed you to the bridge-builder. The Bureau will fetch you at the end of the page; [pause] until then... work.
D18_N_END_CAPTIVE: [formal] Recorded. We're taking you back, Mr Tolga: the Byzantine record resumes on the night of 3 May. [deadpan] Don't return the wet clothes to the Bureau.
D18_T_01_CAPTIVE: [nervous] Master, I'm actually from the other side. I mean... from no side. [weak laugh] I'm in insurance.
D18_T_END_CAPTIVE: [tired] [thoughtful] I built a bridge. For the other side. [softly] But the knots are mine; whoever crosses it, let them cross safely.
D18_U_01_CAPTIVE: [gruff] You're the one they fished out? You're wet, but your hands work. [matter-of-fact] Here prisoners work and Janissaries work; the bread's the same for all.
D18_U_02_CAPTIVE: [puzzled] Insurance? What's that, some kind of prayer? [brisk] Here's the order: barrel pair into the water, lash with rope, lay the planks. Six sections.
D18_U_TAPE: [curious] What's that? Sticky rope? [impressed] ...You wrapped it over the hawser and the knot stayed put. [amazed] They don't have this in Venice.
D18_U_TAPE_2: [amused] Again? [chuckles] Let's hope the Sultan doesn't count the strips when he crosses.
D18_U_TWINS: [amazed] Two Janissaries holding barrels. Never seen it in my life. [pleased] Hold on, then: if the barrel doesn't move, the knot doesn't slip.
D19O_R_HOOKS_BAD: [suspicious] ...Wait a moment. Weren't you the oarsman whose hooks wouldn't hold on Baltaoğlu's galley on 20 April? [cold] Powder's short; two shots are yours, don't waste them.
D19O_R_HOOKS_OK: [impressed] They tell it all over the fleet: on 20 April you were the oarsman whose hook held on Baltaoğlu's galley. [approving] A hand that holds a hook holds a gun; five shots are yours.
D19_C_01_CAPTIVE: [excited] You! They saw you hauling barrels on the Turks' bridge, and you got away. [scheming] You've got Turkish and you know barrels: just our man. If anyone asks, you do the talking.
D19_C_GRAIN_HALF: [conspiratorial] The crew counts your vote as half, Bureau man. [warmly] I've written it down as a whole one anyway.
D19_C_REPORT_TEZKIRE: [hesitant] And... we got past the patrol on this Frank's paper, Niko. [lowered voice] The Sultan's tughra.
D19_C_TEZKIRE: [through gritted teeth] The Sultan's paper, on a Venetian ship. [suspicious] Whose man are you, Bureau man?
D19_C_TEZKIRE_2: [dry] Supplementary cover. The crew saw it. [warning] They won't forget it at the vote.
D19_NK_TEZKIRE: [surprised] Tolga's? [softly] ...Let him keep it. [grave] If the city falls, that paper will save a life.
D19_N_END_TEZKIRE: [formal] Recorded: 3 May to 23 May. The sources say the crew voted to return. No source says an Ottoman patrol bowed to a Venetian ship. [dry] Your footnote is getting longer, Mr Tolga.
D19_P_TEZKIRE: [startled] The Sultan's tughra... [humbly] Forgive us, sir, we didn't know. [respectful] Clear sailing to you!
D19_S2_SAVED: [firm] And there's this: on the night of 28 April this man pulled me out of the Horn. [heartfelt] I owe that city a life.
D19_S2_TEZKIRE_RETURN: [quietly] Leave him be. The man with the paper is going back to die with us. [moved] That's enough for me.
D19_S_GRAIN_BAD: [bitter] One more thing. On 20 April I was on the grain ship, lashed to Cattaneo's carrack. This man was on that deck, and the ship came in wounded. [cold] His vote counts as half to me.
D19_S_GRAIN_FLEE: [vindicated] Even the man who cut the ropes says "save ourselves". You see? I'm not alone.
D19_S_GRAIN_OK: [earnest] One more thing. On 20 April I was on the grain ship, lashed to Cattaneo's carrack. This is the man who cut the grappling ropes. [loyal] I'll vote the way he votes.
D19_S_GRAIN_RETURN: [resolved] The man who cut the ropes says "we go back". Then I go back too. [sad smile] My wife can wait.
D19_S_TEZKIRE: [suspicious] Show us your paper first, Frank. If the Sultan's man says "go back", it's a trap; [darkly] if he says "run", it's worse.
D19_S_TEZKIRE_FLEE: [accusing] See? The Sultan's man doesn't want us back in the city.
D19_T_01_CAPTIVE: [defensive] I didn't escape. I signed a form and a door opened. [sighs] ...Yes, I speak Turkish. [self-deprecating] My experience with disguises still stops at the fez.
D19_T_TEZKIRE: [confident] Captain, bring your lantern over here. [knowing] You'll know the tughra.
D19_T_TEZKIRE_2: [salesman voice] I'm an insurer, captain. I've got a policy with everyone. [smug] This is... supplementary cover.
D20O_T_TAPE: [confident] One moment, master. [proudly] A hairline crack gets a hairline fix.
D20O_U_01_ULIGHTER: [delighted] [shouting] You! The one in the fez! The apprentice who left me his fire box! [proudly] Look, it still strikes. [brisk] Today I need hands.
D20O_U_BED_CROOKED: [worried] Ever since the sled slipped that day, the bed has sat crooked. [firm] Keep your aim tight; a ball that strays even a little won't count.
D20O_U_BED_SOUND: [approving] The bed settled first time that day; you carried the rollers. [warmly] This gun knows your hands; even if it strays a little, it marks the wall.
D20O_U_FLAW: [grave] But listen: I told you those moulds were Serbian work. There's a bubble in the bronze's belly. [ominous] This gun starts the day with a crack.
D20O_U_LESS: [urgent] A cracked barrel doesn't get a full charge. [shouting] Half measure! The ball will fall short: raise the muzzle!
D20O_U_NAME_1: [fond] Look: Monday. You named it; I haven't forgotten. [chuckles] Today's the longest day of the week for the Greeks.
D20O_U_NAME_2: [fond] Look: Parcel. You named it; I haven't forgotten. [hopeful] Hold like the cloth, you said; today we'll see if it holds.
D20O_U_NAME_3: [fond] Look: Insurance. You named it; I haven't forgotten. [laughs] Covers everything, you said; today it covers all the damage to the wall.
D20O_U_NAME_4: [whispers] [conspiratorial] Look: Cube. I told no one; the army calls it 'the Great Gun'. You call it that too.
D20O_U_NAME_GONE: [sad] The gun you named blew up in April, lad; I haven't forgotten. [proud] This is its big brother. [quietly] Nobody names this one.
D20O_U_TAPED: [tense] Tick... Wait. [amazed] It held! [laughs] That sticky strip of yours! Still there. [proudly] The bronze complained, but the strip didn't let go.
D20O_U_TAPE_AGAIN: [amused] More strip? [laughs] Half this gun will be bronze and half your strip.
D20O_U_TAPE_NEW: [skeptical] A sticky strip? ...Will it hold bronze? [listening carefully] [impressed] It holds. I haven't named it, but it holds.
D20_G_01_KNOWN_GBOOK: [warm] The insurance man! [troubled] I read your book. One page keeps me up at night. We'll talk later. [brisk] You came empty-handed; here, empty hands carry.
D20_G_01_KNOWN_GLIGHTER: [warm] The insurance man! [proudly] Your lighter's with me; my gunners light fuses even in the rain. You came empty-handed. Good. [brisk] Here, empty hands carry.
D20_G_01_KNOWN_WARNED: [warm] The insurance man! [wry] Look, the shield's always on my right: I'm minding my right shoulder. You came empty-handed. Good. [brisk] Here, empty hands carry.
D20_G_GUN_GLIGHTER: [urgent] Frank! Take this, it came from Genoa. [grinning] I lit its match with your lighter, first time. [warning] It kicks, keep it on your shoulder!
D20_G_LEON_LOST: [somber] Still no word of Leon, not since April. [quietly] Tonight the breach is one archer short.
D20_G_LEON_OK: [warmly] Leon is at the breach tonight, beside you. [moved] He says he's come to pay his debt.
D20_NK_01: [cheerful] [out of breath] Tolga! I'm off watch tonight; I'll haul the planks, you see to the barrels!
D20_NK_DROP: [straining] One load from me! [encouraging] Don't stop counting, Frank.
D21O_D_LISTEN_K: [impressed] Your ear hasn't forgotten the earth, fez. [chuckles] You'd have made a miner.
D21O_T_LISTEN_FIRST: [whispers] Wait. [listening] Tap... tap... [tense] Someone's digging from the other side, towards us. I heard it just like this in April.
D21_G_01_CAPTIVE: [cool] The scribe who fell off the wall at Blachernae. I'm Johannes Grant. [businesslike] The guards gave you to me: you speak Turkish, so tonight you're my ears, and later my tongue.
D21_G_CAP1_CAPTIVE: [suspicious] You're a Turk, and so is he. Ask him: where are the other tunnels? [threatening] Translate it wrong and I'll know, scribe.
D21_K_CAPTIVE: [bitter] I saw you at Blachernae, scribe. You're the one they threw off the ladder. [contemptuous] Now you speak their tongue?
D21_N_01_CAPTIVE: [over a crackling radio] [dry] Mr Tolga, this page is the Greeks' record and you are a prisoner. The Bureau will fetch you at the end of the page. [firm] Until then, do Grant's work.
D21_N_END_CAPTIVE: [formal] We're taking you back, Mr Tolga: the Ottoman record resumes on the night of 17 May. [deadpan] Grant will be told you escaped.
D21_T_01_CAPTIVE: [nervous] I'm not a scribe. Well, this week I am. [earnest] Really I'm in insurance: I don't take sides, I assess.
D21_T_CAPTIVE_K: [softly] [sincere] I speak both tongues. Tonight they're both asking the same thing: that nobody dies.
D21_T_EAR: [whispers] Hang on. In April, under the ground, I learned to listen. [thoughtful] An ear is a bowl too.
D21_T_THERMOS: [apologetic] Sorry, tea. [determined] I've filled the lid with water; that's the last bowl.
D22O_HU_01: [eager] Wherever Hasan goes, I go. I'm Hüseyin. [proudly] ...This time I'm sure.
D22O_HU_01_HUFEZ: [cheerful] The one in the fez is Hüseyin, that's me. Wherever Hasan goes, I go. [eager] I'll carry baskets and nail hides too.
D22O_HU_CARRY: [coughing] [shouting] The last one's mine! [out of breath] [proud] My eyebrows are gone, but the carpenter's here.
D22O_H_BLAKH_BAD: [gruff] You've been limping since they threw you off the wall at Blachernae, clerk. [warning] You'll carry the basket slowly; when the arrows come, don't be far from cover.
D22O_H_BLAKH_OK: [impressed] You're the clerk who beat the Greek on the wall at Blachernae, aren't you? The company's talking about you. [protective] Tonight I'll shout "Cover!" early when the arrows come; you run early too.
D22O_H_CAPTIVE: [surprised] Scribe! They said the Greeks took you, that you were interpreting in Grant's mine. [relieved] ...Well, you're back. [brisk] The tower's waiting; questions later.
D22_G_BLAKH_BAD: [frustrated] They got onto the wall at Blachernae, clerk; all the good fuse went that night. [warning] These were cut in a hurry: some burn short, some long. Don't take your eyes off them.
D22_G_BLAKH_OK: [proud] Clerk, the Emperor asked about the man who held the wall-walk at Blachernae; I told him it was you. [confident] Tonight his own gunner cut your fuses: they burn evenly, you won't miss the moment.
D22_G_COLOGNE: [sniffs] [puzzled] What's that smell? ...Not wine. [grim satisfaction] Worse than wine. Good.
D22_G_SOAKED: [shouting] [exultant] You let go early, but they couldn't kick it! The cologne barrel rolled down burning and the base caught!
D22_T_COLOGNE: [mischievous] One moment. [proudly] Lemon cologne, eighty proof. Wet hides won't stand up to this.
D23_I_LETTER: [formal] [warm] You're the one who brought the Emperor's April letter to the Sultan. Today's offer is its answer; the Sultan will be pleased it passes through your tongue again.
D23_TH_PASS: [surprised] This... is my feast-day permit! A single seal. [pleased] Now it has two: palace interpreter. [warmly] Look after it until it has seven.
D23_T_PASS: [delighted] I've been promoted. [wry] Seven years in insurance couldn't get me a title; one sheet of paper just did.
D23_T_SINGED: [sheepish] They stayed at the tower. The tower burned, and so did they. [hastily] It won't get in the way of translating.
D24O_K_MENU_1: [proud] Know what's in the pot? Your feast soup: tarhana. [warmly] From the Sultan's table to the army's cauldron.
D24O_K_MENU_2: [proud] Know what's in the pot? Your feast soup: lentil. [warmly] From the Sultan's table to the army's cauldron.
D24O_K_MENU_BURNED: [teasing] I tried the soup you burned at the feast again, in this pot. [chuckles] It didn't burn this time. Neither did the kitchen.
D24O_K_THERMOS: [pleased] I filled that magic flask of yours with soup too; it's been piping hot for three hours. [brisk] I'll take it to the fire nearest the kitchen; you see to the others.
D24O_S_1_THERMOS: [amazed] The head cook's red flask! The moon's going dark, but the soup's still boiling. [relieved] So not everything goes dark.
D24O_S_TEA: [awed] [softly] Hot... [superstitious] That must be why the moon's gone red. It's boiling.
D24O_T_ECLIPSE_AGAIN: [uneasy] I saw this in April too. From a cell in the walls, a month early. [whispers] Is it going dark twice because of me?
D24O_T_TEA: [calm] [warmly] Tea. The moon will wait; it's not going anywhere. Tea goes cold.
D24_NK_01: [earnest] Tolga! I've handed my watch over for an hour. [loyal] I'll walk beside you; if the wind comes, I'll put my shoulder to the pole.
D24_NK_KID: [urgent] [shouting] I'm laying a door across the porch! It'll hold the water back. You fetch the boy!
D24_NK_LATE: [shocked] He ran! ...Uphill, to the dry side. [hopeful] [trembling] He'll make it, Tolga. He'll make it.
D24_NK_SAVED: [out of breath] [relieved] The boy's dry. You're soaked, and so am I. [laughing] But the boy's dry.
D24_T_ECLIPSE: [to himself] [uneasy] They say the moon went dark two nights ago. I saw it a month early, in April, from a cell window. [whispers] Did this city's moon go dark twice, or did I come too early?
D24_T_NK_01: [warm] Niko. Glad you came. [sad] No jokes today, I promised; [soft laugh] so don't make me laugh.
D25_G_TEZKIRE: [shouting] Stop, kitchen boy! [suspicious] ...What's this? [reverent] My Sultan's tughra. Very well. [warning] But I've got my eye on you.
D25_K_CANDLE: [excited] [breathless] Stranger! The stranger from the eaves! I found my mother, she was at the market. [happy] She lit a candle for you too.
D25_K_PASS: [solemn] [warm] The palace interpreter. You carried my words to the Sultan's envoy exactly as I spoke them. [humbly] Forgive me too, Frank.
D25_K_PASS_SOFT: [solemn] [knowing] The palace interpreter. You softened my words a little; I know. [gently] I have forgiven it. [humbly] Forgive me too, Frank.
D25_T_MARCO: [softly] [tender] Don't leave your mother's side tonight, little one. [urgent whisper] Not for a moment.
D26O_AB_LADDER_BAD: [weary] [bitter] Clerk... On 18 April that stockade didn't give us a scratch. This is what's left of my company. [warning] Keep your head down; stones are coming.
D26O_AB_LADDER_OK: [excited] [shouting] Clerk! You were the one who tore the stockade down with a hook on 18 April. We'll hold the top of the ladder; shields up!
D26O_K_WATER: [shouting] [brisk] Frank! The buckets are on me, you're the water-boy. My kitchen boy is watering the first company; you run to the other two!
D26_G_25_BAD: [grim] If you didn't hear it, we don't know. [determined] We'll meet every wave like the first.
D26_G_25_OK: [thoughtful] [calculating] The expendable men first... Then the first of the oil goes to the foot of the ladders; few will make it up the first ladder. [grim] I'll save my best for the Janissaries.
D26_G_DUCK: [gasps] [shaken] ...Frank. A finger lower and... [weak laugh] I owe you a wine.
D26_G_DUCK_GBOOK: [gasps] [shaken] ...That line wasn't in your book, Frank. [wondering] You again.
D26_G_HURT_GBOOK: [pained] [gasping] It went through the breastplate... Your book was right. [weak] Take me... take me to the ship.
D26_G_HURT_WARNED: [pained] My right shoulder... [bitter] You told me in April, Frank. I didn't listen. [weak] Take me to the ship; I'll have it bound and come back.
D26_G_LIGHTER_BACK: [weak] [gentle] Take it. My gunners never paid their week. Neither did I. [sad smile] ...Keep it.
D26_G_NOTRUST_GBOOK: [proud] [defiant] Get down? I read your book, Frank. The twenty-ninth of May, this very spot. [scoffing] Who changes what's written—
D26_G_NOTRUST_WARNED: [irritated] Get down? In April it was my shoulder, now this... [proud] I am Giustiniani, Frank. I do not—
D26_I_KASIM_FREE: [whispers] [trembling] I'm walking out on a miner's word, Frank. I'm nobody now. [relieved] I'm leaving as nobody.
D26_I_TEZ_FREE: [whispers] [wry] It's an honour to be your clerk, Frank. I'm nobody now. [relieved] I'm leaving as nobody.
D26_KS_1: [warm] [excited] Interpreter! Remember me? Kasım. Grant kept his word: the tunnels burned empty, nobody was left inside. [relieved] And this morning our lot opened my cell door.
D26_KS_1_FIRE: [warm] Interpreter! Remember me? Kasım. [sad] Mirko's face is still burned, but he's alive. [relieved] And Grant kept his word: the tunnels burned empty. This morning our lot opened my cell door.
D26_KS_FREE: [firm] [pleading] Agha! This old man is the interpreter's clerk. If I came out of that tunnel alive, it was on this man's word. Let him go.
D26_N_KASIM_FREE: [softly] The sources say he escaped; they don't say how. On a sapper's word... [warm] I won't put this in the file either, Mr Tolga.
D26_N_PHONE_BACK: [formal] One more thing, Mr Tolga: the Bureau's issued phone. The return form's right here. [puzzled] ...Fourteen percent. [deadpan] Always fourteen percent.
D26_N_TEZ_FREE: [softly] The sources say he escaped; they don't say how. ...Now we know. [warm] I won't put this in the file, Mr Tolga.
D26_S_KASIM_FREE: [indifferent] The sapper's interpreter, the interpreter's clerk... Take him. [dismissive] One old man less; nobody's counting.
D26_S_TEZ_FREE: [reverent] My Sultan's tughra... [dismissive] Take your clerk. One old man less; nobody's counting.
D26_T_25_BAD: [apologetic] Last night I got as far as the pavilion, but the guards chased me off twice. [sad] I didn't hear how it ended.
D26_T_25_OK: [urgent] [lowered voice] Last night I was at the back wall of the Turkish pavilion. I heard the Sultan: first the azaps, then the Anatolian troops, last the Janissaries.
D26_T_AYA_CANDLE: [softly] [moved] Last night I lit a candle here. The others have gone out. Mine is still burning. [awed] Soldiers everywhere, and it's burning.
D26_T_KASIM_ASK: [urgent] [quietly] Kasım, that white-bearded man in the column... he's my clerk. [firm] Now you keep a word.
D26_T_LIGHTER_BACK: [softly] [choked up] The lighter's still warm. Forty days in a Genoese pocket.
D26_T_LIGHTER_KEEP: [gentle] [sad smile] No room in the bag. You keep it; you'll light a match on the ship.
D26_T_PHONE_BACK: [wry] I didn't charge it once in a month. [amused] It was always fourteen percent.
D26_T_TEZ_FREE: [firm] [confident] Agha! This old man is my clerk. The Sultan's warrant: here's the tughra, here's my name.
D27_B_1: [warm] [tired] Bureau man! From the brigantine. Twenty days of empty sea, remember? [sad] The city fell. We'd gone back all the same.
D27_B_FLEE: [rueful] You said "save ourselves". You were right. [quietly] I've got a berth on Morosini's ship; nobody's voting this time.
D27_B_RETURN: [proud] You said "go back". I don't regret it. Morosini's offering me a berth, but I'm staying: [determined] every ship that leaves this shore will need a captain.
D27_B_TEZKIRE: [thoughtful] The night you showed that paper with the tughra, nobody in the crew slept. [sad] Now I get it: everyone should have had a paper.
D27_GN_AGAIN: [cool] Keep your ledger well, customs man.
D27_GN_FOUND: [surprised] [wry] The customs man from Rumeli Hisarı! The man who found the fifth item in my hold last August. [chuckles] The one under the hemp.
D27_GN_GO: [bitter] You drank my wine and deleted a line. If the charter's lines get deleted like that too... [resigned] I'm leaving, customs man. For Chios.
D27_GN_MISSED: [smug] The quick customs man from Rumeli Hisarı! Last August you wrote down four items. [dry] The fifth reached Galata; now that's the Sultan's too.
D27_GN_STAY: [respectful] And you wouldn't take my wine. If men like you are going to keep the Sultan's charter, I'm staying. [warm] My ledger stays too.
D27_I_THANKS: [warm] [grateful] The man with the tughra paper. I'm going to Rome. I owe you a prayer, Frank. [chuckles] And a hat.
D27_I_THANKS_KASIM: [moved] A miner's word, an interpreter's tongue... I'm going to Rome, Frank. I owe you a prayer. [softly] And one for Kasım.
D27_N_BRIG: [dry] Recognise the captain at the foot of the gangway, Mr Tolga? You spent twenty days on the same deck.
D27_N_GENOESE: [dry] Look at the Genoese by those chests, Mr Tolga. Last August at Boğazkesen you searched his ship.
D27_N_ISI: [softly] Look at the white beard in the queue for the ship, Mr Tolga. Look familiar?
D27_T_B_FLEE: [warm] Safe travels, captain. [softly] May the wind be behind you this time.
D27_T_B_RETURN: [earnest] Stay, captain. Someone has to meet the ships that come back.
D27_T_GN_GO: [sheepish] One line short, one bottle extra... [sighs] You're right. Safe travels.
D27_T_GN_STAY: [sincere] The declaration was complete. The charter will be read out complete too. [warm] Stay.
D27_T_I_THANKS: [playful] Forget the hat, Cardinal. [chuckles] The red was drawing too much attention anyway.
D28O_U_ROAD_BAD: [worried] The bridge gave way on the Edirne road and the sled's runner cracked. [firm] You'll set the rollers often, clerk, or it slips.
D28O_U_ROAD_OK: [approving] The drovers know you from the road; you got them over that bridge. [confident] The sled won't slip even if you set fewer rollers.
D30O_AZ_WRONG: [panicked] [shouting] Not this way! Very much not this way!
D30O_A_LATE: [out of breath] [triumphant] Made it! Where's the fight? [confused] …Back? [resigned] Right, I'm back too.
D30O_D_CHASE: [shouting] [triumphant] They're running! Push them off the wall!
D30O_G_CAPTIVE: [curious] Is this the scribe who fell off the wall and then carried a wounded man on his back? [impressed] Brave. Does he speak Turkish? [pleased] ...He does. God's grace: I need an interpreter.
D30O_N_CAPTIVE: [over a crackling radio] [concerned] Mr Tolga, your signal is coming from inside the walls. You'll write one page in the Greek record: in Grant's mine. [reassuring] The Bureau will fetch you afterwards.
D30O_T_CAPTIVE: [deadpan] Promoted from scribe to prisoner. [sarcastic] Any change in pay?
D30O_T_DONTLOOK: [nervous] [muttering] Don't look down. Don't look down. [terrified] …Looked.
D30O_T_DOWN_OK: [out of breath] [relieved] I jumped off the last rung and the ladder went over behind me. [wry] First thing tonight that happened on time.
D30O_T_FLOOD: [alarmed] The wall-walk filled up all at once. They keep pouring out of the tower doors, spears pointed at us. [nervous laugh] And we were calling this a win.
D30O_T_PANIC: [panicked] Right, heroics are over. [shouting] Where's the ladder?!
D30O_T_RIDE: [dazed] I didn't bring the ladder down; the ladder brought me down. And there was a bush. [grateful] Bless that bush.
D30O_T_SHOVED: [groaning] Someone shouldered me off the wall. A bush caught me. [wry] Tonight I trust bushes more than people.
D30O_T_WOBBLE: [panicked] [shouting] No no no, leave it! Leave the ladder alone!
D30_D_GUNNER_BAD: [skeptical] Are you the gunner from the Horn? We heard your shot went into the water. [cold] Powder's short; three shots for you.
D30_D_GUNNER_OK: [impressed] Are you the gunner from the Horn? We heard you hit the bridge. [eager] Five shots for you: bring down the ladder-bearers.
D31O_TW_39_BAD: [cold] [resentful] You're the clerk from Petrion. The banner reached our street late; my neighbour's door was broken. If you want rope, knock on another door.
D31O_TW_39_OK: [grateful] Clerk! You're the one who put the banner on our door in time in Petrion. [urgent] Here, our well rope. Lower the child with it.
D31O_T_39_BAD: [sighs] Fair enough. [determined] I'll climb with both hands, then.
D31O_T_39_OK: [warm] A banner saved a door, the door brought a rope. [proud] In insurance that's called reinsurance.
D32O_AZ_25_BUNDLE: [shouting] [encouraging] The Head Cook's lad has already thrown the first bundle. The rest is yours, clerk!
D32O_K_25_BAD: [stern] Last night the guard sent you back to the kitchen twice from behind the pavilion, and he told me too. [lowered voice] I'll tell you how the council ended: fasting today, the assault tomorrow. [firm] No lad for you today; every bundle is yours.
D32O_K_25_OK: [conspiratorial] Last night the guards searched behind the pavilion for an apprentice and never found him. It was you, I know; keep your mouth shut and so will I. [warm] I've sent my lad to the ditch: he'll throw the first bundle.
D32O_TP_01_HIT: [delighted] The lad in the fez! The marksman who split Coco's fusta in two on the Horn! [laughs] Then you turned firefighter. [proud] Today you're a gunner again, and the aim is yours.
D32O_TP_GUNNER: [shouting] [urgent] A gunner on the wall! While the barrel cools, get behind the gabions!
D32O_TP_NAME_1: [curious] Master Urban calls the great gun 'Monday', did you know? Some lad named it. [teasing] Was it you?
D32O_TP_NAME_2: [puzzled] Master Urban calls the great gun 'Parcel'. Whatever that means. Some lad named it. [teasing] Was it you?
D32O_TP_NAME_3: [amused] Master Urban calls the great gun 'Insurance'; apparently it covers everything. Some lad named it. [teasing] Was it you?
D32O_TP_NAME_4: [curious] Master Urban has given the great gun a name, but he won't tell anyone. [probing] Do you know it?
D32O_TP_URBAN_CRACKED: [grim] Master Urban's great gun is silent today: two cracks in the bronze. [pointed] Some impatient lad's doing, they say. This is its little brother; the load falls on it now.
D32O_TP_URBAN_TAPED: [amused] Master Urban's great gun is talking at the next battery, still with your grey strip round its waist. [fond] This is its little brother; it talks less and listens more.
D32O_T_25_BAD: [sheepish] Miss the last five minutes of a meeting and you miss the whole project. [sighs] Same in insurance.
D32O_T_25_OK: [innocent] I heard nothing, Head Cook. [lowered voice] All I know is: fasting today, the assault tomorrow.
D35O_D_HITLOG0: [relieved] [shouting] It hit the trestle! No lashing on it yet, nothing lost. [urgent] Push the next one off with the pole when it's in the ring!
D36_G_01: [lowered voice] [commanding] The Turks are digging a trench fifty paces beyond the moat. They've set wheeled wooden screens in front of it. [determined] Before first light we burn the screens and scatter the diggers.
D36_G_02: [whispers] [firm] Cross on the planks, not a sound. If the drums start, drop whatever you're holding and run back. [grave] No one stays outside.
D36_G_ALL: [relieved] [solemn] Everyone who went out came back. [softly] Tonight God counted the Genoese one by one.
D36_G_BACK: [shouting] [urgent] Back! Everyone to the bridge! The men on the wall will cover you!
D36_G_BURN: [urgent] The diggers have run. Take the torch and set all three screens alight. [shouting] Quickly!
D36_G_LEON: [grief-stricken] [quietly] The sipahis took Leon. I couldn't hold the gate open for him; [bitter] if I had, they'd have taken us all.
D36_G_ORDER: [grave] Orders from the Emperor: from now on no one goes outside the walls. [heavy] Losing one of our men costs more than costing them a thousand.
D36_L_01: [friendly] [confident] I'm Leon, archer. On the way back I'll watch your back, interpreter. Don't worry.
D36_L_HELP: [in pain] [shouting] Interpreter! My leg... an arrow! [desperate] I can't get up!
D36_L_THANKS: [grateful] [out of breath] I owe you, interpreter. Leon doesn't forget a debt.
D36_L_UP: [groaning] Your shoulder... all right. [gritted teeth] Walk, I'll keep up.
D36_N_01: [over a crackling radio] [formal] 9 April 1453, before dawn. The siege has barely begun; the great gun has not fired yet. According to the file, tonight Giustiniani's men go out beyond the walls. [firm] Mr Tolga, you go with them. Observation only.
D36_N_END: [formal] Recorded. 9 April: the sortie. [grave] From now on the Greeks fight only from inside the walls.
D36_N_PHOTO: [over a crackling radio] [urgent] Record frame, Mr Tolga: the burning screens, the walls behind. Be quick, the camp is waking.
D36_T_01: [nervous] [sarcastic] So we're leaving these lovely stone walls of our own free will. Fine. [nervous laugh] Normally I'm the type who locks the door from the inside.
D36_T_BURN_2: [excited] [whispers] Two. Dry wood, pitch-soaked cloth... it goes up nicely.
D36_T_LEON: [guilty] [quietly] I walked right past him. I know.
D36_T_TORCH: [awed] [nervous laugh] A torch. I am holding an actual torch. [anxious] I wonder if this is insured.
D38O_R_01_TOLD: [urgent] [remorseful] Clerk! The eyes before the chain! That night you said "their turbans are wound wrong"; I didn't listen, and twenty days later we missed by an oar's length. [earnest] Tonight, whatever you see, tell me. I'll listen.
D38O_S2_HOOKS_AGAIN: [exasperated] Just like the hooks... [relieved] Never mind, both of them are up.
D38O_S2_HOOKS_BAD: [resentful] Clerk, on 20 April I was on Baltaoğlu's galley too. Your hooks didn't hold; the next day they dismissed the Bey. [stern] The ladder's yours. Make it hold this time.
D38O_S2_HOOKS_EVEN: [grudging respect] It held. I've forgotten the hooks, clerk.
D38O_S2_HOOKS_OK: [warm] Clerk, on 20 April I was on Baltaoğlu's galley too. You were the only oarsman whose hook held that day. [eager] I'll take the ladder's other leg; two hands beat one.
D39O_SA_38_BAD: [hostile] I know you, clerk. When I fell in the water at the Golden Horn you were on the quay writing on your paper; the old man pulled me out. [defiant] Your paper won't stop me today either.
D39O_SA_38_MID: [grudging] You pulled me out of the water, clerk, I'll give you that. But that night the ladder didn't hold and the job was left half done. [stubborn] Step aside; I know this door as well as you.
D39O_SA_38_OK: [hesitant] Wait... that face. You're the clerk who pulled me out from between the quay and the hull at the Golden Horn walls. [sighs] ...Fine. I won't swing. [firm] But you stop my mate.
D39O_SA_TEZ_SULTAN: [stunned] The clerk's name on the Sultan's own paper? [reverent] ...Axes down. We'll wait a while longer.
D39O_TW_PASS: [amazed] This seal... it's Theodoros the Logothete's! The seven-copies man. [relieved] Anyone who got a permit out of him is honest. [eager] Wait, I'll run and fetch the çavuş myself!
